# Iterative hybrid workspace template

A self-contained template for project workspaces that are **human-first with agent acceleration**: the user directs, and agents research, analyze and implement where they are strong, while the user does by hand what they do better (taste, feel, level design, art direction) or wants to own. The direction is known in general but not in detail; it evolves as the project is built, played or used. Plans are written just in time, one handover-sized chunk at a time, and completed plans are kept as a frozen record of what was built and fixed.

Project status, priorities and backlog live in the user's own tracker (for example Trello or Notion). The workspace holds what agents need to work without deviating: the project brief, the conventions, the plans and an append-only history of the order in which the work happened.

Other templates in the family: `AUTONOMOUS_AGENTIC_WORKSPACE_TEMPLATE.md` (agents build end to end against an approved roadmap), `MANUAL_IMPLEMENTATION_WORKSPACE_TEMPLATE.md` (the user implements; the agent coaches) and `AGENTIC_LEARNING_WORKSPACE_TEMPLATE.md` (the agent implements step by step while the user builds along and learns).

## How to use this template

Provide this file to the agent and describe the project: what it is trying to achieve, the platforms and constraints, and whether it is new or existing. For example:

> Read ITERATIVE_HYBRID_WORKSPACE_TEMPLATE.md and use it to set up this project's workspace. Here is what I am trying to achieve: <description>. Preserve existing work. Do not write any plans yet.

**The generated workspace is self-contained.** It never refers to this template or its repository: no provenance note, no links, no copied template text. Everything agents need is written into the project's own files. When the user later asks to bring in material from the template repository (an add-on such as an engine bridge setup, or a stored skill), the agent creates the needed files in the project (see *Add-ons on request*) and the project still does not link back.

The example invocation does not need to be stored in generated documentation.

## Working agreement

- **The user directs.** The user owns priorities, status and the backlog (in their own tracker), taste calls (look, feel, level layout, UX, naming of player- or user-facing things) and changes to the project brief.
- **Who implements is chosen per plan.** When a plan is handed over, the user names the implementer: an agent, the user, or a split by task. Agents implement only plans handed to them and stay inside their scope. When the user implements, the agent reviews on request and does not edit the user's work unless asked.
- **Agents plan on request.** Milestone, feature, implementation, bug-fix and enhancement plans are drafted with the user and approved before work starts (see *Planning*).
- **Agents suggest; the user decides.** Agents propose changes to the brief and the conventions, and candidate skills, at the end of a plan or when they notice the need. Nothing is added to those files without the user's approval.
- **Authorization.** Irreversible, destructive, costly or externally visible actions (publishing, pushing, accounts, purchases, paid API use beyond an agreed budget, deleting work, system-wide changes) need explicit authorization for that action. Git, tool installs and external communication are user-managed unless delegated; a delegation and its boundaries are recorded in `docs/CONVENTIONS.md`.
- **Preserve work.** Do not reset, clean, move or overwrite unrelated material. Completed plans are never edited (see *Planning*).
- **No sub-agents** unless the user or the project's instructions ask for them.
- **The records must stand alone.** Any session can stop and any agent client can resume from the files: the plan being worked on, `docs/plans/HISTORY.md` and the conventions, never from chat memory.

## Bootstrap procedure

1. Inspect what exists: instructions, documentation, code, assets and repository state. For an existing project, identify its layout, stack and the patterns its code already follows before proposing anything.
2. Take the project description from the user. Keep confirmed requirements, assumptions, proposals and open questions distinct. Ask only questions that materially affect the brief or the conventions; do not invent a product, features or preferences.
3. Verify what the agent can verify itself: installed tools and versions, the build, the filesystem. Record only commands that were actually run.
4. Generate the minimum set (see *Workspace structure*): `AGENTS.md`, a client entry file for each agent client the user uses (for Claude Code, `CLAUDE.md` containing `@AGENTS.md`), `docs/PROJECT_BRIEF.md`, `docs/CONVENTIONS.md`, `docs/plans/README.md`, `docs/plans/HISTORY.md` (header only) and `.claude/skills/README.md`.
5. For an existing project, write the patterns observed in the code into `docs/CONVENTIONS.md`, each marked *observed*, and ask the user to confirm or correct them. Keep the project's existing README; it gets no status or plan content.
6. Do not write plans during bootstrap. Offer to draft the first milestone, starting from the brief's riskiest open questions.
7. Finish with the audit (see *Final audit and handoff*).

Scaffolding produces documentation only. Do not create product files, install dependencies, contact external services or initialize source control unless that work is separately requested.

## Workspace structure

```text
<project>/
  AGENTS.md                          How agents work here; read order; boundaries
  CLAUDE.md                          Client entry file: @AGENTS.md (one per client in use)
  docs/
    PROJECT_BRIEF.md                 North star, pillars, constraints, non-goals, open questions
    CONVENTIONS.md                   Patterns and rules agents must follow; grows as patterns settle
    plans/
      README.md                      Plan hierarchy, IDs, types, rules and formats
      HISTORY.md                     Append-only: start / hold / resume / done, in real order
      M00-<slug>/                    Milestone (completed ones are frozen)
        MILESTONE.md
        F01-<slug>/                  Feature
          FEATURE.md
          I01-<slug>.md              Implementation plan: one handover
        B01-<slug>.md                Bug-fix plan (may fix work from an earlier milestone)
        E01-<slug>.md                Enhancement plan
  .claude/
    skills/
      README.md                      What belongs here and how to add a skill; starts empty otherwise
  <code>/                            Wherever the project needs it
```

Preserve an existing project's layout; place `docs/` and `.claude/` beside it and record intentional deviations in `docs/CONVENTIONS.md`. For a workspace of several independent projects, repeat `docs/` per project (for example under `projects/<id>/`) and keep one root `AGENTS.md`; nested `AGENTS.md` files hold only additions.

### Document responsibilities

| Document | Owns | Keep out |
|---|---|---|
| `AGENTS.md` | Working agreement, read order, boundaries, how planning, history, conventions and skills work here | Brief content, conventions, plans, status |
| Client entry files | A pointer to `AGENTS.md`; client-only notes | A copy of `AGENTS.md` |
| `PROJECT_BRIEF.md` | What the project is trying to achieve and why | Status, plans, implementation detail |
| `CONVENTIONS.md` | Rules and patterns agents must follow, verified commands | Status, history, tutorials, long procedures (those become skills) |
| `plans/README.md` | Plan hierarchy, IDs, types, rules, formats | Plan content |
| `plans/HISTORY.md` | The order in which work started, paused, resumed and finished | Status commentary, reasoning (that stays in the plans) |
| Plans | What was planned, how it was verified, what was delivered | Live status (the user's tracker owns it) |
| `.claude/skills/` | Reusable procedures for this project | Rules (those go in `CONVENTIONS.md`) |

Each fact has one home; other documents link to it. Do not generate empty or speculative documents. Soft size budgets: `AGENTS.md` ~8 KB, `PROJECT_BRIEF.md` ~10 KB, `CONVENTIONS.md` ~15 KB (move procedures to skills before splitting), each plan ~15 KB (split before it grows past that).

## Project brief and conventions

**`PROJECT_BRIEF.md`** states the direction, not the roadmap:

- **North star:** one or two sentences on what the project is.
- **Pillars:** three to five qualities every decision is weighed against.
- **Platforms and constraints:** targets, engine or stack, performance budgets, hard limits.
- **Non-goals:** what the project deliberately does not do.
- **Open questions:** ranked by risk, each with what would answer it. Answered questions move out: the answer becomes a pillar, a constraint or a convention, with a pointer to the plan that settled it.

The brief changes as the project does. After a plan whose results bear on the direction (a playtest, a spike, user feedback), the agent proposes the edit and the user approves it.

**`CONVENTIONS.md`** holds what agents must follow so they do not drift from the project's patterns. Group it by topic, for example:

- Layout and naming: folders, files, assets, IDs.
- Architecture rules: module boundaries, data flow, authority and replication models, patterns to use and to avoid.
- Code and asset standards: style, formats, budgets (polygon counts, texture sizes, frame time).
- Verification: the commands for each verification level, each listed only after it has been run here, with the shell it runs in. When the project starts long-running processes (servers, containers, editors), a **Check first** entry says how to see what is running and how to stop it or free a port.
- Repository rules: what is ignored, delegated git operations, branch naming.
- Secrets: where they live (environment variables or a credential store, never the repository or the plans).
- Agent clients in use and where each reads its skills.

Each rule takes one or two lines. A multi-step procedure becomes a skill with a one-line pointer here (see *Skills*). Rules are added when a pattern settles, usually at a plan's wrap-up; the agent proposes them and the user approves. A rule that is replaced is updated in place, and the plan that changed it is named on the rule's line.

## Planning

### Hierarchy and types

| Level | Is | Written |
|---|---|---|
| **Milestone** (`M`) | An outcome the user can play, demo or use, for example "first level playable on Windows" | At the start of the milestone, with the user |
| **Feature** (`F`) | One system or capability inside a milestone; a folder of implementation plans | When the milestone starts, or just before the feature starts |
| **Implementation plan** (`I`) | One chunk of work handed over to an implementer, ending in something checkable | Just before it is worked on, against the code as it stands |
| **Bug-fix plan** (`B`) | A fix to completed work, from this milestone or an earlier one | When the bug is taken on |
| **Enhancement plan** (`E`) | A change to completed work that improves or extends it | When the enhancement is taken on |

A small feature may need only one implementation plan, but it still gets a `FEATURE.md` so every feature reads the same way. A bug or enhancement too large for one handover becomes a feature folder with implementation plans instead of a single `B` or `E` file.

**Spikes** answer one open question before work builds on an assumption (for example: can the target device hold the frame budget; does the networking approach work across platforms). A spike is an implementation plan whose header says `Kind: spike`; its result is a finding, not merged code. The finding goes into the plan's outcome and becomes a brief or conventions proposal. Spike code stays on its branch; building the real thing is a new plan. When the brief has high-risk open questions, propose spikes for them in the first milestone.

### IDs and paths

- Two-digit numbers within the parent: `M00`, `M01` at the top; `F01`, `B01`, `E01` inside a milestone; `I01` inside a feature. Each type numbers on its own.
- Folder and file names add a short kebab-case slug: `M01-first-level-playable/F02-weapons/I01-weapon-framework.md`.
- The full reference is the path of IDs: `M01/F02/I01`, `M02/B01`. Use it in plans, history, commit messages and the user's tracker.
- IDs are never reused or renumbered. A plan that is dropped keeps its file, with the reason in its outcome.

### Rules

1. **Completed plans are frozen.** Once a plan is done, its file and everything under a completed milestone stay unchanged. Later changes are new plans that name what they change (`Fixes: M01/F02/I02`, `Enhances: M01/F02/I01`); searching for an ID finds every later change to it.
2. **New work goes into the current milestone,** wherever the bug or enhancement came from. A milestone is the window of time in which its work was done. The current milestone is the latest one started and not done in `HISTORY.md`. Between milestones, ask the user to start the next one before planning new work; a completed milestone is never reopened.
3. **A plan still in progress is not frozen.** A bug found in it becomes another task in that plan; only completed work gets a `B` or `E` plan.
4. **One plan at a time per implementer** is in progress. Starting another means putting the first on hold in `HISTORY.md`.
5. **Plan just in time.** Do not write future milestones, features or implementation plans in detail; the user's tracker holds the backlog. Before authoring, verify what can be verified (the code, the environment, the tools).
6. **Size for one handover.** An implementation plan is completed and verified in one session or a few, and ends in something the user can check. Split it before authoring when it would not.
7. **Plans are agent-neutral.** They name files, commands and outcomes, not client-specific tool names, so any agent client, or the user, can carry them out.
8. **Never narrow scope or acceptance silently.** A change to what a plan delivers is agreed with the user and noted in the plan.

## Plan formats

`docs/plans/README.md` carries these formats, adapted to the project. Plans hold no live status; task checkboxes exist so any session can resume the work.

**`MILESTONE.md`**

```markdown
# M01 — [Title]

🎯 Outcome — [what the user can play, demo or use when this milestone is done]
📦 Scope — ✔ in · ✖ out
✅ Done when — [observable checks, including the user's own playtest or review]

## Features
- F01 — [title] — [one line]
- F02 — [title] — [one line]

## Notes
[Risks, open questions this milestone answers, links to the brief.]

## Outcome
[Filled when the milestone is done: what is now true, what moved to later milestones, brief or convention changes it led to.]
```

**`FEATURE.md`**

```markdown
# M01/F02 — [Title]

🎯 Goal — [what the feature does, one or two lines]
🧭 Design — [key choices, data shapes, interfaces; link the brief or conventions instead of repeating them]
📦 Scope — ✔ in · ✖ out

## Implementation plans
- I01 — [title] — [one line]
- I02 — [title] — [one line; planned later]

## Outcome
[Filled when the feature is done.]
```

**Implementation plan (`I01-<slug>.md`)**

```markdown
# M01/F02/I01 — [Title]
Kind: build | spike · Implementer: agent | user | split · Depends: [IDs or —]

🎯 Goal — [the checkable result]
📚 Context — [links to FEATURE.md, the brief, conventions, related plans; files to read first]
📦 Scope — ✔ in · ✖ out

## Tasks
- [ ] T1 — [title] · files: [paths] · verify: [command or check] → [expected]
- [ ] T2 — …

✅ Done when — [what is true when the plan is complete; the user's check if one is needed]

## Outcome
[Filled at the end: what changed (files, commits), evidence (see *Verification and evidence*), deviations from the plan and why, findings, follow-ups for the user's tracker, proposed convention, brief or skill changes.]
```

**Bug-fix plan (`B01-<slug>.md`)**

```markdown
# M02/B01 — [Title]
Fixes: M01/F02/I02 · Found: YYYY-MM-DD · Implementer: agent | user | split

🐞 Problem — [what happens] · Expected — [what should happen]
🔁 Repro — 1. … 2. … 3. …
🔍 Cause — [filled once found]

## Tasks
- [ ] T1 — [title] · files: [paths] · verify: [command or check] → [expected]
- [ ] T2 — Regression check: [the repro no longer reproduces; the original plan's checks still pass]

## Outcome
[As in an implementation plan.]
```

**Enhancement plan (`E01-<slug>.md`)**

```markdown
# M02/E01 — [Title]
Enhances: M01/F02/I01 · Implementer: agent | user | split

💡 Why — [what is lacking and what prompted it: playtest, feedback, a later feature]
🔧 Change — [what will be different]

## Tasks
- [ ] T1 — [title] · files: [paths] · verify: [command or check] → [expected]

## Outcome
[As in an implementation plan.]
```

Markers: `🎯` goal or outcome, `🧭` design, `📦` scope, `📚` context, `✅` done when, `🐞` problem, `🔁` repro, `🔍` cause, `💡` why, `🔧` change; tasks `[ ]` open, `[x]` done, `[~]` dropped with a reason on the line.

## Working a plan

1. **Plan.** The agent reads `PROJECT_BRIEF.md`, `CONVENTIONS.md`, the parent milestone and feature, related completed plans and the code involved; asks what it needs; drafts the plan. The user refines and approves it.
2. **Hand over.** The user names the implementer in the plan header. An agent starts in a fresh session when the planning conversation was long; the plan must carry everything the work needs.
3. **Start.** Append a `start` line to `HISTORY.md`.
4. **Implement.** Follow the tasks in order, verify each one, tick it, and keep notes for the outcome. Stop and ask the user when: the plan is ambiguous or contradicts the brief or conventions; the work needs a taste call; scope would change; it needs credentials, an account, spend or a destructive action; or the same check has failed three times.
5. **Review.** The user reviews, plays or uses the result. Fixes found now are new tasks in the same plan.
6. **Wrap up.** Fill the outcome; append a `done` line to `HISTORY.md`; propose any convention, brief or skill changes and apply the ones the user approves. When the last plan of a feature or milestone is done, fill its outcome and append its `done` line too.

**Hold and resume.** To switch to other work, note in the plan where it stopped (an unticked task with a short note), append a `hold` line with the reason, and start the other work. To resume, append `resume` and continue from the first unticked task after rereading the plan and anything changed since the hold.

## History

`docs/plans/HISTORY.md` is the record of the order in which work happened, including work paused for something else and resumed later. The user's tracker keeps live status; this file is only the record.

```text
# History
Append-only. One line per event, oldest first: date · event · plan ID · note.

2026-11-02  start   M02          Stealth AI
2026-11-02  start   M02/F01      Guard perception
2026-11-02  start   M02/F01/I01  Sight cone
2026-11-04  done    M02/F01/I01
2026-11-04  start   M02/F01/I02  Hearing
2026-11-05  hold    M02/F01/I02  Waiting on recoil fix
2026-11-05  start   M02/B01      Rifle recoil desync (fixes M01/F02/I02)
2026-11-06  done    M02/B01
2026-11-06  resume  M02/F01/I02
```

- Events: `start`, `hold`, `resume`, `done`, `dropped` (with the reason in the note).
- The agent appends a line when work it is doing changes state, and when the user reports their own work changing state. The user can also append lines by hand.
- Never edit or delete a line. A mistake is corrected by a new `note` line naming the line it corrects.
- Notes are a few words; reasoning stays in the plan.

## Verification and evidence

Every task names how it is verified, using the cheapest check that settles the claim. Three levels; `CONVENTIONS.md` gives the project's exact commands:

| Level | When | Typical content |
|---|---|---|
| **Fast** | Every change | Build, lint and format, static and data validation, unit tests |
| **Standard** | Behavior changes | Fast plus functional or integration tests, including networked or multi-process checks when the behavior spans processes, and checks through an editor or tool bridge where one is set up |
| **Full** | End of a milestone, demos, platform targets | Standard plus multi-client runs, performance budgets on target hardware, visual captures, packaging; then the user's own check |

Outcome evidence keeps these apart:

1. **Executed:** commands or actions actually run, with the result and any artifact path.
2. **Inspected:** what was read or reviewed and what it supports.
3. **User-reported:** what the user says they checked, attributed to them.
4. **Not checked:** what could not be checked, and why.

- A planned check is never reported as executed. Generated or configured is not the same as working.
- Feel, look and layout are judged by the user; the agent supplies captures and measurements, not the verdict.
- Visual defects: reproduce first, then fix, and close on a before and after capture where the tooling allows.

## Skills

`.claude/skills/` holds this project's reusable procedures as Agent Skills. It starts with only a `README.md`; skills are added when the project shows it needs them.

**When to suggest one.** The agent suggests a skill when a multi-step procedure has been done more than once or was hard to work out and will recur. For example: how to verify a feature through the engine editor's MCP bridge after implementing it; how to import and validate a generated 3D model; how to run and read a profiling capture on the target device. The suggestion gives the name, when it would be used and an outline of the steps. A skill is created only when the user approves.

**Rules or procedures.** A rule ("all gameplay state is server-authoritative") goes in `CONVENTIONS.md`. A procedure (the steps to check replication in a two-client session) becomes a skill, with a one-line pointer from `CONVENTIONS.md`.

**Format.** One folder per skill, `.claude/skills/<name>/SKILL.md`, with YAML frontmatter and a markdown body; supporting scripts or examples sit beside it:

```markdown
---
name: <kebab-case-name>
description: <what it does and when to use it, in one or two sentences; agents choose skills from this line>
---

# <Title>

<When to use it, prerequisites, then numbered steps with exact commands and the expected results.>
```

Keep skills specific to this project: real paths, real commands, verified results. Update a skill when its procedure changes; remove one that is no longer used. `.claude/skills/` is where Claude Code reads skills; if another agent client is in use, record in `CONVENTIONS.md` where it reads them and keep one copy of each skill.

Copying a skill to another project or to the template repository happens only when the user asks.

**`.claude/skills/README.md`** says what belongs in the folder, repeats the format above and the rule that skills are added with the user's approval.

## AGENTS.md and client entry files

The generated `AGENTS.md` is the single source of agent rules. It contains, concisely and with paths that exist in this project:

1. One line on what the project is, linking `docs/PROJECT_BRIEF.md`.
2. **Read order** at the start of a session: `docs/PROJECT_BRIEF.md` → `docs/CONVENTIONS.md` → `docs/plans/README.md` → the last lines of `docs/plans/HISTORY.md` → the plan being worked on, its feature and milestone.
3. The working agreement (see *Working agreement*) and authorization boundaries, including any repository delegation.
4. How planning works: the hierarchy, IDs, the rules, just-in-time authoring, with a pointer to `docs/plans/README.md` for the formats.
5. Working a plan, hold and resume, and the history rule.
6. Verification levels and evidence, with a pointer to the commands in `docs/CONVENTIONS.md`.
7. When to propose convention, brief and skill changes, and that nothing is added without the user's approval.
8. That project status lives in the user's tracker, not in the repository.

It does not repeat the brief, the conventions or the plan formats, and it does not mention the template.

**Client entry files.** A client that does not read `AGENTS.md` natively gets a thin entry file pointing to it, never a copy. For Claude Code: `CLAUDE.md` containing `@AGENTS.md`, plus client-only notes if any. Create entry files only for the clients the user uses. Tool-server (MCP) configuration is per client and per project (for example `.mcp.json` for Claude Code, `opencode.json` for OpenCode); when more than one client is in use, keep their entries equivalent.

## Final audit and handoff

Before reporting the workspace ready, check:

- The brief captures what the user supplied without invented scope; assumptions and open questions are marked as such.
- For an existing project, observed conventions are marked *observed* and put to the user.
- Only the files listed in *Workspace structure* were created; no status, roadmap, session or empty documents.
- Nothing refers to the template or its repository.
- `AGENTS.md` is concise, its read order uses real paths, and client entry files point to it.
- `docs/plans/README.md` carries the hierarchy, IDs, rules and formats; `HISTORY.md` has its header and no events.
- Commands in `CONVENTIONS.md` were actually run here; anything unverified is labelled.
- Links resolve; tables and code fences are valid.

Finish with links to `AGENTS.md`, `docs/PROJECT_BRIEF.md` and `docs/CONVENTIONS.md`; say what was created or adapted and what was verified; offer to draft the first milestone.

## Add-ons on request

The template repository has optional add-ons for specific tooling. They are not used during bootstrap. When the user asks to apply one, read it and create what the project needs in the project itself:

- Configuration files (MCP entries, scripts) in the project, at the paths the add-on gives.
- Rules and verified commands in `CONVENTIONS.md`.
- Repeatable procedures as skills, with the user's approval (see *Skills*).

The add-ons were written for the other templates in the family, whose workspaces keep `MEMORY.md`, tooling notes and a roadmap. Map their instructions to this structure: tooling notes and conventions → `CONVENTIONS.md` or a skill; decisions → the plan's outcome or a convention; plan-level steps → tasks in the current plan. The project does not link back to the add-on.

| Add-on | Use when |
|---|---|
| `UNREAL_MCP_BRIDGE.md` | An Unreal Engine project where agents should inspect or edit the editor |
| `UNREAL_TEST_AUTOMATION.md` | An Unreal Engine project with automated checks at each verification level |
| `BLENDER_MCP_BRIDGE.md` | Blender scene work or batch asset pipelines |
| `ASSET_GENERATION_PIPELINE.md` | 3D assets or reference images are sourced or generated (packs, AI 3D, Blender), with provenance and licences |
| `AGENT_ORCHESTRATION.md` | A cheaper worker agent client carries out implementation plans dispatched by an orchestrating agent |
